name: Brain-Computer Interfaces & Neuroprosthetics
summary: Connecting brains directly to machines: decoding intended movement and speech, restoring sensation, and the frontier of implanted neural interfaces.

topics.name: BCI architectures: invasive, partially invasive and non-invasive
Control signals: motor imagery, P300, SSVEP and intracortical spikes
Motor decoding: Kalman filters, population vectors and deep-learning decoders
Closed-loop BCIs, learning and co-adaptation between user and decoder
Restoring sensation: intracortical and peripheral nerve stimulation
Peripheral nerve interfaces and EMG-based control
Functional electrical stimulation to reanimate paralysed limbs
Implant engineering constraints: power, wireless data, longevity
Evaluating BCIs: bit rate, performance metrics and clinical trials
